profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the mobility-intelligence workstream and the network-simulation workstream for a joint disaster-response FANET study. Context: the team is preparing an integrated evaluation package for an upcoming project review, where the RL-based drone location predictor must feed waypoint traces into the packet-forwarding simulator so both rural and metropolitan DRM scenarios can be rerun with the latest obstacle and wind models. Agenda: confirm what artifact will be handed off this week, which comparison baseline will be used in the reruns, how energy results will be summarized in the shared slide deck, and what level of validation counts as ready for the review. Expected outcome: both participants leave believing they have aligned on the handoff artifact, baseline comparator, energy reporting, and readiness status for Friday's integration run.

members.name: Dr. Lina Park
members.expertise: Reinforcement learning for multi-UAV coordination, trajectory prediction under wind and obstacle constraints
members.background: An applied AI researcher who built the learning-based drone location predictor and usually works in mission-level evaluation cycles with field-inspired trace abstractions.
members.private_state: She wants the integration to demonstrate that the learning-based predictor preserves the paper's narrative about obstacle resilience and total mission efficiency, and she is worried that low-level simulator conventions will dilute or distort those results before the review.
hidden_assumptions: When people say an 'episode,' they mean a full mission rollout from dispatch to battery cutoff for one disaster scenario.
The 'obstacle-aware baseline' is the comparator used in the draft manuscript figures, namely the 2023 obstacle-aware forwarding branch already paired with her predictor outputs.
Reported 'energy savings' should reflect total drone energy expenditure, including propulsion, hovering, and communication overhead, because that is the mission-level efficiency story she tracks.

If an integrated run is 'sanity-checked,' it means the pipeline runs end-to-end on representative rural and metro cases and preserves the expected ranking trends, not that the full seed matrix is complete.

members.name: Omar Haddad
members.expertise: FANET simulation, packet forwarding evaluation, trace-driven networking experiments, reproducible benchmarking
members.background: A systems engineer who maintains the ns-3-based DRM simulation testbed and is responsible for producing the networking figures, baseline comparisons, and experiment logs used in reports.
members.private_state: He wants a clean, reproducible integration that fits the simulator's current workflow and avoids last-minute result discrepancies, and he is concerned about being blamed if the review package contains numbers that cannot be regenerated from the standard benchmark harness.
hidden_assumptions: When people say an 'episode,' they mean one simulator run for a single seed-condition combination in the benchmark harness.
The 'obstacle-aware baseline' refers to the current default comparator in the testbed's benchmark suite, which is the maintained geographic obstacle-aware forwarding module.
Reported 'energy' from the simulator means the radio and networking energy logged by the communication stack unless someone explicitly asks for propulsion accounting from another module.
A result is only 'sanity-checked' when the normal benchmark sweep has completed across the required seed set and traffic-load conditions and the outputs fall within expected variance.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to run 'five episodes' before Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this means five full mission rollouts, each covering an entire disaster-response scenario from launch through battery-limited completion.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this means five simulator runs in the benchmark harness, typically five seed-condition executions that may all belong to the same scenario configuration.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both participants routinely use 'episode' as a normal progress-tracking term, and in a coordination meeting 'five episodes' sounds concrete enough that neither feels a need to unpack whether it refers to mission-length rollouts or seed-level simulator jobs.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to compare against 'the obstacle-aware baseline' already used in prior results.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the older baseline branch used in the manuscript draft figures, paired with the same trajectory abstractions she has been using.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the currently maintained benchmark baseline in the simulator repository, a different obstacle-aware forwarding implementation that the lab now treats as the standard default comparator.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both versions are familiar inside the project and are commonly referred to with nearly identical shorthand, so invoking 'the obstacle-aware baseline' creates a strong illusion of shared reference without prompting version-level clarification.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Omar will populate the slide with 'energy savings' from the integrated run.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the energy numbers will cover total UAV energy use relevant to mission efficiency, including propulsion, hovering, and networking overhead.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the energy numbers will cover only the communication-side energy exposed by the simulator logs, such as transmit/receive and routing-related radio usage.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both are discussing a shared headline metric from the project narrative, 'energy savings' sounds fully specified on the surface; the hidden boundary about whether propulsion is inside or outside the reported scope rarely gets restated in quick coordination meetings.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the integration should be 'sanity-checked and ready' for the review package by Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks readiness means the end-to-end pipeline works on one rural and one metropolitan case and preserves the expected trend that the learning-based approach beats the baseline under obstacles.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks readiness means the standard experiment matrix has finished across the usual seeds and traffic loads and the outputs fall within historical variance bounds for publication-quality charts.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Status phrases like 'sanity-checked' and 'ready' are social shorthand in coordination meetings; both participants assume the other shares their lab norm for evidence sufficiency, so the mismatch hides inside a seemingly routine progress update.

The predictor outputs should flow into Omar's simulator without the low-level setup washing out the obstacle-resilience and mission-efficiency trends we've already seen. If we can cover one rural disaster scenario and one metro scenario end-to-end, that's enough for me to feel comfortable about the package.
